headline: Supreme Court green-lights Trump’s expanded SAVE citizenship database for voter-roll checks; Bitget revises hack to ~$387.5M and suspects North Korea; Vercel’s skills.sh hits 1M agent skills.

stories.title: SCOTUS lets Trump admin use expanded SAVE database for voter-roll checks
facts: Supreme Court Fri (6–3, conservatives in majority): emergency stay lets the Trump administration use an expanded SAVE citizenship database as states check voter rolls.

SAVE (1986 benefits tool) was bulk-expanded with Social Security data after a March 2025 EO; challengers (League of Women Voters et al.) say it is unreliable and risks flagging newly naturalized citizens.
Unsigned majority: NVRA still bars broad purges in the weeks before an election, “limits the potential impact” this year; federal law requires responding to state citizenship queries.
Jackson dissent: even a few disenfranchised lawful voters outweigh the government’s claimed injury; Texas ran 18M+ registrations through SAVE — only three illegal-voting charges.
stories.whyItMatters: Highest-court green light for a contested citizenship-matching tool weeks before midterms — with the court stressing the NVRA’s near-election purge ban as a partial brake.

image.alt: U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin

stories.title: Bitget hack revised to ~$387.5M; CEO points at North Korea patterns
facts: Bitget support update (Fri): on-chain accounting now ~$387.5M to attacker addresses (was $351.6M) after adding Zcash + TRON transfers — not further outflows; incident “contained.”
Attack path: backend wallet system spoofed transfer data and triggered auth signing; private keys / cold wallets ruled out; withdrawals still paused (status target Sep 26 04:00 UTC).
CEO Gracy Chen / CNBC: preliminary IP/VPN patterns match prior North Korean ops; Mandiant + SlowMist assisting; User Protection Fund >$464M said to cover losses.
Recovery bounty: 5% of frozen and 5% of recovered funds; live tracing dashboard published; Bybit LazarusBounty channel used.
stories.whyItMatters: One of the year’s larger exchange heists, with attribution still provisional and withdrawals gated until Bitget finishes validation.

stories.title: Vercel: skills.sh hits 1M agent skills and ~280M installs in seven months
facts: Vercel blog (Fri): skills.sh registry crossed 1M unique skills and ~280M installs seven months after launch (Agent Skills debuted Oct 2025; registry three months later).

Supply vs demand: >½ of listings are technical (eng/agents/data/infra/security), but >⅘ of installs go outside pure software engineering — business ops, writing, cloud over-index on installs per listing.
Concentration: top 375 skills (0.04%) = 62% of installs; top 1.2% = 94%; no single skill >1% share. Cross-industry skills = 87.5% of installs.
Thesis: next million skills will encode company-specific judgment; quality should shift from install counts toward effectiveness tests.
stories.whyItMatters: Official registry census of the agent-skills market — useful baseline as Cursor/Claude/OpenAI ecosystems keep shipping skill formats.

stories.title: NYT: Netanyahu kept alleged UAE Oct. 7 warning out of Oct. 1 Gaza briefing
facts: NYT via ynet (Fri): minutes of an Oct. 1, 2023 Gaza security meeting show Netanyahu did not mention an alleged late-Sep call from UAE President MBZ warning Hamas was considering a major attack.
Five former senior Israeli officials told the Times the Emirati warning never reached security chiefs or later internal Oct. 7 probes; warning itself was vague (rocket vs ground unclear).
PMO denies any such warning/call; prior Times of Israel Emirati source had confirmed a phone warning. Meeting focus: keep Gaza calm; Netanyahu cautioned escalation could hurt Saudi normalization.
stories.whyItMatters: Adds a contemporaneous-minutes angle to the pre–Oct. 7 warning dispute ahead of Israel’s election — still contested by the PMO.
